narasi: Why does honey never spoil? Honey has very little water, is naturally acidic, and contains compounds that slow bacteria. Microbes cannot grow in it. Archaeologists have reported ancient honey from old tombs that was still preserved after thousands of years. Follow for more facts.

teks: How similar is our DNA to a chimpanzee's?
narasi: How similar is our DNA to a chimpanzee's? Humans share roughly 98 to 99 percent of their DNA with chimpanzees. The small differences, especially in how genes are switched on and off, add up to big differences in brains and behavior. Follow for more facts.

label: Daily Fact Bites
teks: Are you looking at the past when you look at stars?
narasi: Are you looking at the past when you look at stars? Yes. Starlight takes years to travel to us. The light from a star 100 light-years away left it 100 years ago, so you see the star as it was then. Some stars you see may have changed since. Follow for more facts.

label: Daily Fact Bites
teks: Is the Moon moving away from Earth?
narasi: Is the Moon moving away from Earth? Yes, by about 3.8 centimeters a year, roughly the speed your fingernails grow. Tides transfer energy to the Moon and slowly push it into a higher orbit. Follow for more facts.

label: Daily Fact Bites
teks: How hot is the center of the Earth?
narasi: How hot is the center of the Earth? The inner core is estimated to be around 5,000 to 6,000 degrees Celsius, about as hot as the surface of the Sun. It stays solid because of the immense pressure from all the layers above. Follow for more facts.

label: Daily Fact Bites
teks: How big is a blue whale's heart?
narasi: How big is a blue whale's heart? A blue whale's heart can weigh around 180 kilograms, about as much as a few adults. It beats slowly, only a handful of times per minute when diving, and pumps blood through huge vessels. Follow for more facts.

label: Daily Fact Bites
narasi: Are sharks older than trees? Yes. Sharks have existed for more than 400 million years, while the first true trees appeared roughly 350 to 385 million years ago. Sharks have survived several mass extinctions. Follow for more facts.

label: Pawsome Facts
teks: Why do giraffes have such long necks?
narasi: Why do giraffes have such long necks? A giraffe's long neck helps it reach leaves other animals can't, and males also use their necks to fight. Surprisingly, a giraffe has seven neck bones, the same number as humans. Each bone is just enormous. Follow for more animal facts.

label: Pawsome Facts
narasi: How do bees make honey? Bees collect nectar, store it in a special honey stomach, and pass it from bee to bee, adding enzymes. Then they fan it with their wings to evaporate water until it thickens into honey and seal it with wax. Follow for more animal facts.

label: Pawsome Facts
teks: Can a starfish regrow its arms?
narasi: Can a starfish regrow its arms? Many sea stars can regrow lost arms. In some species, a single arm with part of the central body can even grow into a whole new sea star, although regrowing can take months to a year. Follow for more animal facts.

label: Pawsome Facts
narasi: Why do camels have humps? A camel's hump stores fat, not water. The fat is an energy reserve for long trips without food. Camels survive without water mainly because their bodies lose very little of it and they can drink a huge amount at once. Follow for more animal facts.
